gloss: getting caught up in; being involved; collateral damage

definitions.gloss: getting caught up in; being involved in (something negative)
definitions.explanation: Being drawn into a troublesome situation, conflict, or accident without originally being a party to it. Often implies innocent involvement in someone else's problem.

examples.english: I got caught up in their fight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えになった⟦{通行人|つうこうにん}→通行人：28570_tsuukounin⟧がいた。
examples.english: There were passersby who got caught up in the accident.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧よう、⟦{距離|きょり}→距離：05331_kyori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いている→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: I'm keeping my distance so I don't get involved.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{巻|ま}き (winding, wrapping - from ⟦{巻|ま}く→巻く：02418_maku⟧) + {添|ぞ}え (accompanying - from ⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧)

The image is of being "wound up" or "wrapped into" something.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|く}う→食う：02657_kuu⟧ - to get caught up in (passive involvement)
- {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ - to become involved
- {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ - to drag someone into
- {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{避|さ}ける→避ける：02109_sakeru⟧ - to avoid getting involved

USAGE:
Always negative - implies:
- Unwilling involvement
- Innocent third party affected
- Unfortunate circumstance
- Collateral damage
- ⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught in an accident
- ⟦{争|あらそ}い→争い：09992_arasoi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught in a dispute
- ⟦{犯罪|はんざい}→犯罪：03569_hanzai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - implicated in a crime
- ⟦リストラ→リストラ：04689_risutora⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught up in layoffs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦とばっちり→とばっちり：07726_tobacchiri⟧ - splash damage, undeserved consequence
- ⟦{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる→巻き込む：05753_makikomu⟧ - to be drawn into
- {飛|と}び{火|び} - spreading (of trouble)
- {累|るい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{及|およ}ぶ→及ぶ：01921_oyobu⟧ - to suffer consequences (formal)

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in everyday conversation and news reports.
